profile.summary: A single-laboratory study that reclassified 121 BRCA1 and BRCA2 variants of uncertain significance (VUS) from 120 patients in two steps: first with the standard ACMG/AMP system, current SVI recommendations and new data, then with the ClinGen ENIGMA expert panel specifications on the same data. It reports how many VUS each step moved to benign or likely benign. It is relevant to clinical variant scientists choosing classification rules for BRCA1 and BRCA2, not to model comparison.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: How far gene-specific expert panel rules change the classification of existing VUS compared with the general ACMG/AMP rules, when both are applied to the same up-to-date evidence. The endpoint is the share of VUS reclassified, and in which direction.

quotes.text: We investigated the differences in reclassification between the ENIGMA specifications and the standard ACMG/AMP classification system in a clinical setting.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: 121 VUS (40 in BRCA1, 81 in BRCA2) classified between January 2018 and November 2023 were taken from the laboratory's internal database. These were reclassified in two steps (t2 and t3) from the original classification (t1). All reclassifications were done by one experienced variant analyst. Both steps used the Tavtigian point-based scoring system, but the ENIGMA rules require -2 points for likely benign.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Step t2 applies the standard ACMG/AMP system with SVI recommendations as of November 2023 to the latest annotations. Step t3 applies the ENIGMA specifications version 1.1.0 to the same new data. The study counts VUS moved to likely benign or benign at each step: 20% (n = 24) at t2 and 83.5% at t3, with none moved to likely pathogenic or pathogenic. There is no external truth set; the authors attribute most of the difference to the ENIGMA BP1_STR code, applied to 93 variants.
